intro: Weeaproinah is a forest locality high in the Otway Ranges of Victoria, among the cool temperate rainforest where myrtle beech and tree ferns fill the wet gullies. A reader sent us one of its trees: a myrtle beech whose long limb is lined with kangaroo ferns, moss and lichen, photographed from high among its branches near the Otway Fly Treetop Walk.

trees.story:
"A Myrtle Beech hosting a whole ecosystem of mosses, lichen and kangaroo ferns in the Otways," wrote the reader who sent us this tree from the rainforest of the Otway Ranges in Victoria.

Myrtle beech, Nothofagus cunninghamii, is the beech of the cool, wet rainforest gullies of Victoria and Tasmania, a southern beech whose relatives grow in New Zealand and South America. Where the air stays damp all year its bark and limbs become ground for other plants, and this one has taken that further than most.

The reader's photographs show a long limb running out sideways from a mossy trunk, and along its whole length stand ranks of kangaroo fern, narrow leathery fronds upright like the teeth of a comb. Moss lies thick on the top of the branch and grey lichen crusts the bark. The pictures look down past the limb onto the crowns of tree ferns in the gully below, as if taken from high among the branches.

Their fix falls in the forest about 700 metres from the entrance of the Otway Fly Treetop Walk. We do not know the tree's age or girth; if you do, tell us here.

Look along the limb and count how many ferns have made their home on it.
